Explain a comparison by its key columns

Source: R/explain.R
diff_explain.Rd

Which values of the key columns separate the rows that match from the ones that do not. After diff_table() reports differences, the next question is usually where: one region, one load date, one measure. This answers it from the result alone.

diff_explain(d, column = NULL, among = c("all", "joined"))

Arguments

d

A result of diff_table().

column

NULL (the default) for the overview of every key column, or one column to break down by value: a key column, in either spelling, or "metric".

among

"all" (the default) counts every record; "joined" only those of rows found in both tables.

Value

A data.table. The overview has column, n_values, same_only, differ_only and mixed (the number of values of each class), separates and identifies. The breakdown has the column's values, n, n_same, n_changed, n_only_x, n_only_y and class.

Details

Called with no column, it returns one row per key column, and per metric when the result has measures. Each distinct value of the column is classed by the records that hold it: same when every one of them matches, differ when none does, mixed otherwise. A column separates the result when no value is mixed: knowing the value tells whether the record matches.

A column that holds a different value on every row (an id) always separates and explains nothing; it is marked identifies and ranked last. The others come first, fewest mixed values first, then fewest values: the shortest explanation leads.

Called with a column, it returns one row per value of that column, with its counts of each status, most differences first: the values to look at.

What is counted

For a key column the unit is the row: a row matches only when every one of its measures does, as in diff_report(). With duplicates = "aggregate" the unit is the key. For metric the unit is the value, one per row and measure, so it can say that only one measure changes.

A row found in only one table and a value that changed usually have different causes. among = "joined" counts only the rows found in both tables, so the explanation is of the changed values alone.

Examples

x <- data.frame(
  id = 1:4,
  region = c("north", "south", "east", "west"),
  amount = c(100, 200, 300, 400)
)
y <- data.frame(
  id = c(1:3, 5L),
  region = c("north", "south", "east", "north"),
  amount = c(100, 200.5, 300, 500)
)
d <- diff_table(x, y, by = c("id", "region"))
diff_explain(d)
#>    column n_values same_only differ_only mixed separates identifies
#>    <char>    <int>     <int>       <int> <int>    <lgcl>     <lgcl>
#> 1: metric        1         0           0     1     FALSE      FALSE
#> 2: REGION        4         1           2     1     FALSE      FALSE
#> 3:     ID        5         2           3     0      TRUE       TRUE
diff_explain(d, "region")
#>    REGION     n n_same n_changed n_only_x n_only_y  class
#>    <char> <int>  <int>     <int>    <int>    <int> <char>
#> 1:  south     1      0         1        0        0 differ
#> 2:   west     1      0         0        1        0 differ
#> 3:  north     2      1         0        0        1  mixed
#> 4:   east     1      1         0        0        0   same
diff_explain(d, "region", among = "joined")
#>    REGION     n n_same n_changed n_only_x n_only_y  class
#>    <char> <int>  <int>     <int>    <int>    <int> <char>
#> 1:  south     1      0         1        0        0 differ
#> 2:   east     1      1         0        0        0   same
#> 3:  north     1      1         0        0        0   same
